system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Status:** Draft analysis for the Wattlebridge deal team. Not cleared, not agreed. The Seller's "FINAL" and "settled at principal level" labels, and its "market standard" assertions, do not bind us (playbook §0.4/§6.3). Nothing in this memo is a concession. Facts are as the Seller's Disclosure Letter presents them, dated 22 September 2026. They need refreshing before we rely on them, and NSW law points should be confirmed by counsel.

## 1. Summary of departures

| Area | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m start. 20% is a fallback usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority naming the draft | Departs. Number matches fallback, but no authority exists. Do not treat as cleared |
| De minimis / basket (12.2) | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible-style basket (excess only) | AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k basket, first-dollar once exceeded | Materially worse for Buyer. Seller would absorb far more loss |
| General time limit (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months needs Frost written approval | Departs. No approval given |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Reject outright |
| Limitations/reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, non-waivable | Reject. Must carve out fraud |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Excludes matters known to Buyer/advisers, including anything "discoverable" from data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject. Data-room discoverability is effectively constructive knowledge |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure | Reject |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" | Effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion | Reject |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Reject |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow) | AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller", not in funds flow | Specific line item or seller-funded; on-costs must be captured; no silent exclusion | Reject |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180k unverified either way | Reject the "adequate" characterisation |
| DD-006 export/privacy | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand | Do not accept the materiality conclusion. Keep the matter open |
| Sandbar renewals | "Ordinary-course" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Assess. Don't accept or reject the characterisation yet |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution | Reject. Keep categories separate |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source only | Reject as proof of title |

## 2. Reasoning on the material issues

**Caps, baskets and time limits (12.1–13).** The Seller's cover note says its numbers are "standard" and "widely accepted". That is an assertion, not a reason, and we should not accept it. The 20% cap happens to equal our fallback figure, but the playbook fallback is conditional on Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given. Accepting the number in the Seller's framing would mean conceding a fallback we have not authorised. The basket structure is also a significant shift: a AUD 250k excess-only basket means the Buyer bears the first AUD 250k of aggregate losses. Our structure is AUD 50k, then the Seller pays from the first dollar.

**Fundamental and Title claims.** This is the most significant structural problem. Capacity and title warranties are the core of what we are buying. Putting them under a 20% cap, a basket and an 18-month limit would leave title defects largely uncompensated. The playbook requires a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.

**Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 and the fraud carve-out.** The Seller's "all claims of any nature" language would cover fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. Those must sit outside all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one on our side can waive that carve-out.

**Buyer knowledge (8.3) and data-room deemed disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2).** Read together, these two provisions would let the Seller say we are deemed to know, and have disclosed against, everything in a data room of undefined scope. The "discoverable from public records" language makes it worse. We need specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties. Any knowledge qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and it must not reach title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).** This is a material customer. The Seller says it has not included a final written consent or evidence that the conditions in 11.3 are satisfied, and it offers only reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery. Those positions fall short of the playbook. We need effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion. A reasonable-endeavours obligation alone is insufficient.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m outstanding).** The Seller proposes a post-Completion release. The playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion. If any release has to follow Completion, it needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. We should not fund AUD 3.2m of Seller debt on the Seller's word alone.

**Bonuses (AUD 420k) and funds flow.** The Seller's disclosure says the bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment. It does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply. Excluding them from the funds flow would leave an unpriced liability that we would effectively inherit. We need either a specific line item or Seller funding, with on-costs captured.

**Ironquay (AUD 180k).** The Seller calls its SOW3-only indemnity "adequate". The playbook calls for a broader indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure mechanism. The AUD 180k figure is recorded as open in DD-010, but the disclosure states this is not bank verification of non-payment. We should neither assume the debt is unpaid nor accept that it has been settled. Verify before pricing.

**DD-006 export/privacy (~1,240 records).** The Seller says the matter is "not expected to be material". The Disclosure Letter itself says the investigation is preliminary, the scope is unknown and notification status is unresolved. Our position is to assume neither a confirmed breach nor a notification duty, and not to attach a numeric demand. We should, however, require log preservation, a completed investigation and regular updates before signing. Given the personal-data content (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps), privacy counsel should assess the position before we accept any materiality conclusion.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k).** The three renewals are described as read together for timing and scope, and the disclosure does not say whether each is unavoidable or terminable. We should assess them, but should not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct them from price.

**Tax, IP and Title.** The Seller says the tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime". They are not. Those categories remain open, and we should not assume unlimited liability or resolution. On title, DD-012 is the Company's own register, supplied by the Seller. It is a useful starting point but not independent proof. We need an independent ASIC extract, searches and evidence of the Seller's authority to sell.

**Other items the Seller has not addressed in playbook terms.** The office lease (DD-007) notification obligation and the Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009) may require counterparty consents or notices. The disclosure says neither is a requirement for consent to the share sale, but that is the Seller's characterisation. We should confirm each against the underlying documents and treat any consent as a condition if required.

## 3. Recommendations

1. **Do not accept the Seller's "final", "settled" or "market standard" framing.** Respond that the draft is open for negotiation, and that positions will move only through our internal authority process.
2. **Caps and time limits:** Hold the 25% / AUD 6.0m general cap and the 24-month general period. Any move to 20% / AUD 4.8m or 18 months requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. None has been given.
3. **Baskets:** Counter with a AUD 5k de minimis and a AUD 50k first-dollar basket.
4. **Fundamental/Title:** Reject the Seller's proposal to treat title and capacity as general warranties. Insist on a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Fraud:** Insist on a carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
6. **Knowledge and disclosure:** Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion in 8.3 and the whole-data-room and public-register disclosure in DL 1.1–1.2 and Schedule 7. Require specific disclosure against identified warranties.
7. **Bluefen:** Require effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours-only drafting.
8. **Riverlark:** Require a current payout letter, repayment from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
9. **Bonuses:** Require the AUD 420k, plus triggered on-costs, as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, with no silent exclusion.
10. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity beyond SOW3, preserve the cure mechanism, and verify the AUD 180k position independently.
11. **DD-006:** Require log preservation, a completed investigation and regular updates. Do not accept "not material" and do not assert a breach. Refer to privacy counsel.
12. **Sandbar:** Complete the assessment of the three renewals. No automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
13. **Tax and IP:** Keep these categories open and separate from the general regime.
14. **Title:** Obtain independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. Treat DD-012 as an internal source only.
15. **Lease and Mossvale:** Verify the underlying consent and notice requirements before accepting the Seller's characterisation.
16. **Refresh:** Update all facts. The Disclosure Letter is as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026.
=== END ADVICE ===
